nodes.label: Event Library
nodes.description: Technical library for event definitions, historical searches, visual candidate review, and future detector candidates.

nodes.label: PM_Accepted_Extension_Break_Event
nodes.description: Draft premarket event where an initial extension is accepted in an elevated shelf and later breaks violently.

nodes.label: MOMENTUM_EXPANSION
nodes.description: Family assigned to the draft event.

nodes.label: premarket
nodes.description: Session scope required by the current event definition.

nodes.label: initial_extension
nodes.description: Early premarket extension that marks a first relevant high and shows early attention.

nodes.label: accepted_price_shelf
nodes.description: Elevated price zone sustained after the first extension without a full reversal.

nodes.label: violent_shelf_break
nodes.description: Break of the accepted shelf with multiple expanding one-minute bars.

nodes.label: first bar of violent break
nodes.description: Official event timestamp rule for this draft event.

nodes.label: event_context_start
nodes.description: Conceptual start of the first extension or prior context.

nodes.label: shelf_start_ts
nodes.description: Conceptual start timestamp for the acceptance shelf.

nodes.label: initial_extension_pct
nodes.description: Initial research parameter for percent rise from early premarket base or low to first relevant high.

nodes.label: shelf_duration_minutes
nodes.description: Initial research parameter for minimum and maximum duration of accepted elevated price.

nodes.label: max_extension_giveback_pct
nodes.description: Initial research parameter for how much of the first extension may be given back.

nodes.label: impulse_window_bars
nodes.description: Initial research parameter for the number of one-minute bars in the break impulse.

nodes.label: impulse_push_pct
nodes.description: Initial research parameter for additional price expansion during the violent break.

nodes.label: required observable conditions
nodes.description: Required conceptual conditions such as initial extension, accepted shelf, violent break, rising highs, and threshold push.

nodes.label: optional observable conditions
nodes.description: Optional context such as volume expansion, flat or positive shelf slope, support touches, spread, and catalyst context.

nodes.label: identity and time features
nodes.description: Candidate identity and time fields including ticker, symbol, exchange, date, timestamps, and session segment.

nodes.label: initial extension features
nodes.description: Candidate fields for extension start, high, low, percent move, duration, and volume.

nodes.label: shelf acceptance features
nodes.description: Candidate fields for shelf timestamps, range, slope, drift, support touches, volume, and retained extension.

nodes.label: violent break features
nodes.description: Candidate fields for break window, OHLC, push, volume ratio, rising highs, strong closes, and new high over shelf.

nodes.label: market context features
nodes.description: Candidate context fields including premarket volume, RVOL proxy, gap, market cap, float, spread proxy, halts, and news context.

nodes.label: candidate quality states
nodes.description: Future row states including good, review, degraded, blocked, and invalid candidate.

nodes.label: PM accepted extension review flags
nodes.description: Conceptual flags for clarity, ambiguity, sparse data, halt overlap, split risk, and manual review.

nodes.label: single spike without acceptance
nodes.description: Case that should not be classified as this event.

nodes.label: direct opening push without shelf
nodes.description: Case that should not be classified as this event.

nodes.label: initial extension mostly reverted
nodes.description: Case where the first extension gives back almost all of the move.

nodes.label: clearly downtrending base
nodes.description: Case where the base drifts strongly downward rather than showing accepted price.

nodes.label: visual review checklist
nodes.description: Human checklist for reviewing candidate cases and avoiding event/entry confusion.

nodes.label: detector_candidate
nodes.description: Future maturity status that the event cannot reach yet because key definitions and tests remain open.

nodes.label: Event Library Restructuring Plan v0.1
nodes.description: Planning note for making the Event Library more technical, precise, deduplicated, and reproducible.

nodes.label: v0_capture
nodes.description: Initial unclassified capture state for provisional event definitions.

nodes.label: promoted event
nodes.description: Named and classified event state after enough differentiation and cleanup.

nodes.label: numbered root event file
nodes.description: Root-level numbered file such as 001.md, 002.md, or 003.md used during v0 capture.

nodes.label: family event folder
nodes.description: Final family folder with a named event directory, EVENT.md, notebook, and image folder.

nodes.label: Strategy Library
nodes.description: Library for operational responses and strategy-level notebooks.

nodes.label: Gap and Go
nodes.description: Recommended first pilot strategy for decomposing human strategy into observable events.

nodes.label: strategy notebook
nodes.description: Notebook role for finding samples of a complete strategy and generating visual cases for decomposition.

nodes.label: event notebook
nodes.description: Notebook role for event-level searches, visual candidate review, and comparison of examples.

nodes.label: event_case_explorer.ipynb
nodes.description: Associated notebook name expected for promoted events.

nodes.label: historical search contract
nodes.description: Machine-readable search contract for event id, grain, scope, anchor, data source, columns, parameters, conditions, exclusions, and flags.

nodes.label: candidate row contract
nodes.description: Expected row fields emitted by exploratory event search scripts.

nodes.label: same sequence, fields, and anchor deduplication rule
nodes.description: Rule that events with the same sequence, fields, and temporal anchor are probably aliases or subtypes.

nodes.label: component
nodes.description: Reusable piece of a market phenomenon, such as push, pullback, reclaim, or volume expansion.

nodes.label: top-level event
nodes.description: Observable sequence with enough structure and identity to be treated as an event.

nodes.label: First_3Bar_Push_Event
nodes.description: Related provisional event that may overlap through impulse components.

nodes.label: Gap_And_Go_Event
nodes.description: Related event example used in overlap and deduplication discussion.

nodes.label: DAS_Event
nodes.description: Related event example used in overlap and final-structure examples.

nodes.label: VWAP_Reclaim_Event
nodes.description: Related event example used in overlap and deduplication discussion.

nodes.label: Event Behavioral Mechanics Guide v0.1
nodes.description: Draft policy candidate for documenting trader psychology, game theory, crowd dynamics, and microstructure inside event definitions.

nodes.label: behavioral or microstructural hypothesis
nodes.description: Hypothesis allowed in event definitions only when separated from certainty and operational action.

nodes.label: observable phenomenon
nodes.description: Layer for what happened in the market.

nodes.label: mechanical hypothesis
nodes.description: Layer for why the observed market behavior might occur.

nodes.label: measurable evidence
nodes.description: Layer for how the mechanism can be approximated with observable data.

nodes.label: strategy
nodes.description: Layer for operational action, which is excluded from Event Library definitions.

nodes.label: game-theoretic pressure
nodes.description: Falsable incentive model for participants, actions, information, payoffs, constraints, levels, and measurable proxies.

nodes.label: Pressure Payoff Model
nodes.description: Permitted starting model for estimating latent group pressure from loss, level breaks, volume acceleration, and liquidity.

nodes.label: Sequential Trigger Game
nodes.description: Permitted starting model for representing events as phases and transitions.

nodes.label: Mean-Field Feedback Game
nodes.description: Permitted starting model for aggregate pressure, liquidity, and impact feedback.

nodes.label: GAME_THEORETIC_PRESSURE_FOR_EVENT_SEARCH_ALPHAEVOLVE_v0_1.md
nodes.description: Referenced R&D document for first mathematical formalization of game-theoretic pressure for event search and AlphaEvolve.
